title: Made a multi-view sprite generator(GPT) for a starting point for 2d game dev. Sprite Me Baby!
author: Mekkablood

comments.author: Mekkablood
comments.body:
Thought this might be useful for some. Not always perfect but if you put in the same prompt a few time or change it up a bit usually you'll get something useful. Great starting point for a 2d game.

It requires the subscription version of Chatgpt [https://chat.openai.com/g/g-liOqpzb4E-sprite-me-baby](https://chat.openai.com/g/g-liOqpzb4E-sprite-me-baby)

replies.author: cantbebothered67836
replies.body: Ooohh your post sounds so wholesome and innocent! I can't wait until AI becomes good enough to come up with better game concepts and story ideas than people so people who are gleeful AI is making artists obsolete can feel the same pain.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body:
I'm a 3d modeler, and it's already starting to produce great models for that too. Every white collar job you can think of including ceo's it's coming for.

This is going to be a rough transition, but on the other side you'll be able to curate your own 3d worlds and games. We're entering an entirely new world where just about anything you can think up can be possible. People had this same reaction when photoshop started becoming popular in the 90's.

I can understand your hate and fear, but try to think about what could come out on the other side.

replies.author: cantbebothered67836
replies.body: You're essentially talking about a society almost exclusively made of endorphin addicted consumers, that you can tell an AI what you want to play or watch hardly counts as creative agency. This is the kind of stuff you see in dystopian fiction and we're already sick, sick puppies as it is. No, it's nothing like photoshop. Photoshop opened up a completely new kind of art that runs along side drawn/painted art which is recognizably and entirely distinct (unless you're literally talking about painting on a tablet instead of on a physical canvas in which case the talent of a painter is not outworn).

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: It's similar to photoshop in the reaction people had, obviously this is on another level. The largest point I'd make is it's not about what you or I want, it's about what's going to happen, and trying to find a way to adjust.

replies.author: cantbebothered67836
replies.body:
People who want this to happen will tell you that it will inevitably happen and we should accept and adapt. It's rhetoric or shilling. If you already accept that we can't change things then, yeah, I suppose things won't change. But the demoralization tactic itself is just that, a tactic. 

Look, I get it too. This shit is exciting. I'm an aspiring gamedev, just thinking about the possibilities AI could unlock for game development  and what I could do with it makes me drool. But then I remember about the costs and that we *must* take a principled stance on something like this, the benefits ultimately pale when compared to the pitfalls.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Technology doesn't go backwards, people will eventually flock to whatever gives them the best content.

replies.author: Anxious_Blacksmith88
replies.body: This is not similar to Photoshop. It is the literal death of art for the rest of time.

replies.author: Fraxcat
replies.body: And then you look up and realize the only thing on TV is "Ow, my balls!"

replies.author: Lost_Cheetah_8497
replies.body: You're not getting it. AI is an assistant. For example, this guy wants to make a game, he can now get AI to assist him with designing the characters. He can make games, but he can't draw. That's how a lot of people are going to use AI - to help in their skill gaps. The best stories, whether that's a movie, a game, a book, a sitcom are still going to be written by humans. AI might help them refine it, but the best stuff is always gong to have a human at the helm

replies.author: cantbebothered67836
replies.body:
There's already a way to compensate for your lack of skill in a certain department and it has existed for at least thousands of years, it's called working with someone else. You can pay them or team up with them for free, there are a multitude of incentives you can use to attract talent. If you don't have the dedication to achieve this then you probably didn't have the required dedication to even finish an AI "assisted" game let alone make a good game that's worth a player's time. 

What you describe is not an assistant. An assistant helps the artist with things he/she are already doing, they supplement the artist's work. "Finish coloring this lineart" or "make a rough sculpture and I'll put in the finishing touches". You're talking about **commissioning** content! That's what a promot is. You tell the software what you want it to do for you because you don't have the ability or the will to do it by yourself. This is what the money guy does, not an artist in need of assistance. 

You may conflate that role with that of a "director" rather than a CEO, but what happens when AI becomes good enough, and it will, to "assist" even the job of a "director". What happens when human talent and agency is almost entirely unneeded. What happens to those poor, poor, talentless aspiring devs who can't actually do much but gosh darn it they have dreams! And ideas! No wait the AI has a better idea, nevermind, we'll just do that. You know what, why don't you just, you know, just make a cool game for me DevNet 9000, I don't know, something good, you know better than me. I'll just go masturbate to furry porn and contemplate jumping off the roof, holler when you're done.

replies.author: Lost_Cheetah_8497
replies.body: Its 2023 and things are changing. You don't have to like it, but face facts, things change. Processes change. Jobs change. Society changes. Just 30 years ago the thought that someone could record an album entirely at home that is brilliant sound quality was unthinkable. Recording software can instantly do things that took studios hours/days to achieve and a team of people. You getting all angry about AI is only gonna make you look very very very very old.............. Best of luck

comments.author: asdfghjkl15436
comments.body: Tried it with some simple top down sprites, yeah, this is almost useable. Obviously its a bit blurry and the pixels can sometimes blend together, but given time this is some super interesting stuff.

comments.author: tinman_inacan

This will be very useful for me! Thank you for making this, I can't wait to try it out. 

You probably can't use this for a game you intend to put up for sale on, say, Steam. But if you're just trying to prototype some stuff out or make tech demos not for general release, this should help a lot!!

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: Can always tweak it a little to make it your own, or use as a reference, and frankly the only way steam will know is if you tell them. The Epic store and [itch.io](https://itch.io) will also not have an issue with using ai.
